title: Halting on the final transition
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean-input Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $s$ be a natural-number window radius, and let $\mathrm{upd}$ be an update rule on an accumulator type $T$ and an optional Boolean. Suppose $\sigma$ assigns an accumulator to every Boolean word and satisfies $\sigma(u\mathbin{++}b)=\mathrm{upd}(\sigma(u),b)$ for every word $u$ and optional Boolean $b$, where appending an absent Boolean leaves $u$ unchanged. If, for a time $t$, initial configuration $c$, and Boolean $b$, the run is halted at time $t+1$, the transition from time $t$ emits $b$, and all configurations through time $t+1$ lie in the radius-$s$ window, then the window run with clock $t+2$ halts and returns the configuration at time $t+1$ together with the accumulator obtained by applying $\sigma$ to the time-$t$ output followed by $b$.
